item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00403","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C17","C05","C10"],"selected_candidate_label":"C17","confidence":0.97,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C17 is the strongest reusable template because it combines the same two principal functions later combined in the child: terminating earlier bilateral trade-agreement proclamations and supplementing tariff treatment under multilateral trade agreements. Its recital sequence—original agreement and proclamation, intergovernmental agreement to terminate, satisfaction of relevant conditions, statutory termination authority, then operative termination by a specified close-of-day date—is materially reproduced for Mexico. The child also follows C17's multipart organization, placing termination and quota action in Part I and using later parts to implement other trade-agreement consequences. C05 is also very strong for the child's repeated list-amendment provisions and is expressly incorporated into the child's chain of supplemental proclamations. C10 provides a close single-country termination form, but lacks the child's broader multipart administrative machinery.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"Whereas the Government of the United States has agreed with the Government of the United Mexican States that the said trade agreement shall cease to be effective after December 31, 1950; ... Whereas the final sentence of said section 350(a) authorizes the President ... to terminate in whole or in part any trade-agreement proclamation","parent_excerpt":"Whereas, the Government of the United States has agreed with the Government of the Kingdom of Sweden that the said trade agreement ... shall be terminated after June 30, 1950; ... Whereas the said section 350(a) ... authorizes the President to terminate any proclamation carrying out a trade agreement","explanation":"C17 supplies the same substantive recital sequence and statutory machinery, adapted from Sweden and other countries to Mexico."},{"child_excerpt":"The said proclamations of December 28, and 31, 1942, relating to the said trade agreement with the United Mexican States, shall be terminated in whole as of the close of December 31, 1950.","parent_excerpt":"The said proclamation of July 8, 1935, which proclaimed the trade agreement with the Kingdom of Sweden is hereby terminated as of the close of June 30, 1950.","explanation":"The operative termination formula is closely parallel, including identification of the earlier proclamation and termination at the close of a specified date."},{"child_excerpt":"PART I ... [termination and quota provisions] ... PART II To the end that the said trade agreement ... may be carried out ... PART III To the end that the said exclusive trade agreement ... may be carried out","parent_excerpt":"PART I ... [three termination provisions] ... PART II To the end that the said trade agreement ... may be carried out, that not more than 3,571,429 pounds of butter ... shall be dutiable","explanation":"Both proclamations combine termination and tariff-quota or tariff-implementation actions in a multipart operative structure."},{"child_excerpt":"To the end that the said exclusive trade agreement specified in the ninth recital of this proclamation may be carried out, the list set forth in the ninth recital of the said proclamation of January 1, 1948, as amended and rectified, shall ... be further amended in the manner indicated in the eleventh recital","parent_excerpt":"To the end that the said exclusive trade agreement specified in the fifth recital of this proclamation may be carried out, the list set forth in the ninth recital of the said proclamation of January 1, 1948, as amended and rectified, shall ... be further amended in the manner indicated in the ninth recital","explanation":"This near-verbatim list-amendment formula from C05 is reused in the child, supporting the same broader drafting lineage even though C17 is the best overall template."}]}
